title: Designing Experiments for External Decision Makers
abstract: arXiv:2610.22032v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Standard Bayesian experimental design (BED) methods assume the experimenter alone will act on the data, choosing the best action given their own beliefs and goals. In practice, data are often acted on by external parties whose procedures the experimenter cannot change and may not know, particularly when the data are released publicly. To extend BED to such settings, we introduce usage-aware experimental design, a framework in which an adaptive design policy is trained to minimise the usage risk: the experimenter's expected loss when one or more external rules act on the collected data. These rules may be non-Bayesian or black-box, and when several may apply, we either average over them or take the worst case. We show that, unlike in standard BED, more informative data can be harmful under such rules, so the usage risk cannot in general be expressed as an expected uncertainty reduction; our framework thus strictly generalises standard B

translated_title: 为外部决策者设计实验
translated_abstract: 标准的贝叶斯实验设计（BED）方法假设实验者本人会依据数据采取行动，即基于自身的信念和目标选择最优行动。但在实践中，数据往往由外部各方来使用，其处理流程是实验者无法改变且可能并不了解的，尤其是当数据被公开发布时。为了将BED扩展到此类场景，我们提出了“使用感知实验设计”框架，通过训练自适应设计策略来最小化“使用风险”，即当一条或多条外部规则作用于所收集数据时实验者的期望损失。这些规则可能是非贝叶斯的或黑盒的；当可能有多条规则适用时，我们或对所有规则取平均，或采用最坏情况。我们证明，与标准BED不同，在此类规则下更具信息量的数据可能是有害的，因此使用风险通常无法表示为期望不确定性缩减；我们的框架因此严格推广了标准BED。
tldr: 提出“使用感知实验设计”框架，通过训练自适应设计策略最小化“使用风险”，以应对数据将被实验者无法控制的外部规则（可能是非贝叶斯或黑盒）使用的情况，并揭示在此类场景下更具信息量的数据反而可能有害。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces usage-aware experimental design, a framework that trains adaptive design policies to minimize usage risk when collected data will be acted on by external, possibly non-Bayesian or black-box rules, and shows that more informative data can be harmful in such settings.
